column1: # Taglish spelling and affix variants, mapped to a single lemma token.
# Tagalog marks verbs with affixes, so one root appears in many surface forms:
# "uminit", "umiinit", "nag-init" and "mainit" are four unrelated tokens to a
# word n-gram model even though all four report heat. With roughly 100-140 true
# safety reviews in the whole project, splitting the evidence across four tokens
# would leave none of them above the minimum support threshold. Mapping them to
# WHY A TABLE AND NOT A STEMMER
# There is no maintained Tagalog stemmer for Python, and a general one would
# also collapse pairs that must stay apart (see the "sabog" note below). A table
# is auditable, a native speaker can extend it without touching code, and it is
# hashed into the round manifest so a change after labelling is detectable.
# COLUMNS  variant <TAB> lemma <TAB> kind <TAB> language <TAB> added_by <TAB> added_at
# Matching is per whitespace token, after elongation collapse and casefolding.
# Multi-word phrases are NOT handled here; they belong in the smoke-term list.
# DELIBERATE OMISSIONS - do not add these without re-reading the note:
#   sabog / sumabog   Kept apart on purpose. "sumabog" means exploded, but bare
#                     "sabog" in these reviews usually means scattered or muddy,
#                     as in "sabog ang sound". Merging them would import a known
#                     false friend straight into the safety class.
#   d -> hindi        Real Filipino SMS shorthand, but bare "d" also appears in
#                     English review text ("vitamin d", "type d"). The existing
#                     clean_risk_text() makes this mapping; it is not repeated
#                     here because the precision cost outweighs the recall gain.
#   mainit            IS mapped, even though "mainit sa balat" is a false friend
#                     for cosmetics. That is a hazard-context problem, solved by
#                     the context-token requirement, not a morphology problem.
